tip_title: Your Life Insurance Number Probably Needs a Check-Up
topic: Life Insurance - How Much Coverage Do You Actually Need
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Your Life Insurance Number Probably Needs a Check-Up**

Most people land on a life insurance coverage amount once and never revisit it. But your savings, your debts, your income, and your family situation have probably shifted since you first bought the policy. A number that made sense five years ago might leave real gaps today, especially if you've taken on a mortgage, added a dependent, or changed jobs.

The rough check is simple: add up what you owe (mortgage, car loans, other debt), factor in what your household would need to replace your income for several years, and see if your current coverage still holds up against that number. For a lot of households, it doesn't.

Not sure where your number stands? Your Peachy agent can walk through it with you in plain terms, no calculator required.

📖 [Learn more from Forbes Advisor](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/life-insurance/how-much-life-insurance-do-you-really-need/)
summary: Covers life insurance coverage adequacy as a periodic review item, framed around how debts, income, and family changes since policy inception can leave existing coverage amounts outdated. Distinct from prior tips focused on income-replacement formula, college funding gap, estate settlement costs, and open-enrollment-triggered review.
scoring_notes: Both audiences skew toward life stages where coverage amounts go stale fast: East Cobb has established families and empty nesters who may have bought policies when kids were young; Perimeter has young families and professionals whose financial pictures are actively changing; Lewisville Lake is family-heavy with mixed income brackets and a wide age range. October is a natural financial review month alongside open enrollment season, making this a strong seasonal anchor even though the topic is evergreen. Source is Forbes Advisor (trusted domain). Prior life insurance tips covered income-replacement formula, college funding gap, estate settlement costs, open-enrollment trigger, beneficiary review, and term vs. whole comparison — this tip's angle is the standalone coverage-amount check as a periodic review habit driven by life changes, which is a meaningfully distinct frame. Forbes Advisor is a trusted source per the skill's domain list.
